answer: Duplicate text is easy to catch; duplicate thinking is harder, so answers are clustered by meaning, and a submission that lands too close to an existing one earns nothing even when the wording differs. A farm that paraphrases one insight a thousand times produces a spiral tightening around a single point, and the cluster exposes it faster than any hash would. Honest work adds a new branch, like a cedar rising from the same soil without sharing the trunk, and each dawn brings a fresh prompt so the map of meaning has to keep growing.
